_comment: Issue #214: a remote audiobook release is its parts. The two verbs that turn a release's file list into a book -- KEEP the audio, ORDER it naturally -- plus the token the queue files each part under. Subject is the header-only src/core/RemoteAudiobook.h; probe_remotebook asserts it.

mutants.name: order-lexicographic-not-natural
mutants._why: THE reported defect, restated as a mutation: a plain string compare puts '10 - part' before '2 - part', so a fifteen-hour book starts at part ten. This is the mutant the ordering assertions exist for.

mutants.name: order-not-applied-at-all
mutants._why: Taking the source's listing order verbatim. Debrid lists a release however it likes, which is precisely what 'whatever the source returned first' meant in the three reports.

mutants.name: filter-dropped-every-file-queued
mutants._why: The other direction: cover.jpg, the .nfo and the .epub end up in the queue, so the listener gets silence in the middle of the book -- or, for an ebook release, a player over an EPUB, which is #207's exact report.

mutants.name: filter-keeps-anything-with-an-extension
mutants._why: A blacklist-shaped rule instead of the whitelist. It looks harmless and passes the obvious cases; it queues the next unfamiliar file type there is.

mutants.name: surrounding-space-not-trimmed
mutants._why: A packer's stray whitespace makes the suffix 'mp3 ', which matches nothing, so a whole book's parts read as non-audio and the release refuses with 'no audio files in it'.

mutants.name: a-row-with-no-base-name-renders-blank
mutants._why: A dotfile has no base name; without the fallback the now-playing list shows an empty row where a part should be.

mutants.name: a-part-with-no-id-is-queued
mutants._why: Nothing can mint a link for it, so it is a queue row that can only fail -- the dead-player failure this whole issue is about, one row deep.

mutants.name: token-forgets-which-book-it-belongs-to
mutants._why: Two books whose parts are both called 01.mp3 would then share a resume row -- one book's position recorded against another's, which is the bug #194 and #203 each fixed one instance of.

mutants.name: token-round-trip-loses-the-file
mutants._why: The half the mint reads: a token whose file name cannot be recovered names no file in the release, and the part resolves to nothing.

mutants.name: a-plain-url-reads-as-a-part-token
mutants._why: The choke point routes on this. If an ordinary stream url answered true, every audio stream in the app would be sent off to be re-minted as a book part and nothing would play.
